passages.t: ‘He is holy’: the King who answered Moses, Aaron and Samuel
passages.happening:
Psalm 99 has no heading. It is the last of the run of psalms in Book Four that sing ‘The LORD reigns’. “The LORD reigns; let the nations tremble! He is enthroned above the cherubim; let the earth quake” (verse 1).

The psalm has three parts, and each ends with the same words. “Let them praise Your great and awesome name”, it says, “He is holy” (verse 3). “Exalt the LORD our God, and worship at His footstool; He is holy” (verse 5). And at the end, longer: “for the LORD our God is holy” (verse 9).

The King is just. “The mighty King loves justice” (verse 4).

Then the psalm remembers three people. “Moses and Aaron were among His priests; Samuel was among those who called on His name. They called to the LORD and He answered” (verse 6). God spoke to them from the cloud (verse 7). “O LORD our God, You answered them. You were a forgiving God to them, yet an avenger of their misdeeds” (verse 8).
passages.hearers:
‘Enthroned above the cherubim’ (verse 1) points to the ark of the covenant. On its lid stood two gold cherubim, winged figures. The space above them was pictured as God's throne, and the ark was his ‘footstool’ (verse 5). No statue of God sat there. To the eye the throne was empty. In a world full of statues of gods, that was startling.

Moses, Aaron and Samuel were remembered as great men of prayer. Moses prayed for the people after the golden calf, and “the LORD relented” (Exodus 32:14). Samuel told the people, “far be it from me that I should sin against the LORD by ceasing to pray for you” (1 Samuel 12:23).

Verse 8 says two things about the same people. God forgave them, and he also dealt with their sin. The wilderness stories show both. Moses and Aaron stayed God's servants, but they were not allowed to lead the people into the land (Numbers 20:12). Forgiveness healed the bond. It did not erase every result of what was done.
passages.later:
Isaiah heard the angels around God's throne calling, “Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of Hosts; all the earth is full of His glory” (Isaiah 6:3). Revelation hears the same song in heaven (Revelation 4:8).

Peter writes, “Be holy, because I am holy” (1 Peter 1:16).
passages.asks:
Psalm 99 says ‘He is holy’ three times. Holy means set apart, different from us, pure and good beyond all our ideas. Do you think of God as someone you can approach casually, or as the holy King? Psalm 99 holds both: he is holy, and he answers when people call.

Who prays for you, the way Moses and Samuel prayed for their people? And who are you praying for?
